sonnet.q1: A message on the `domain-events` queue starts ingest. The outbox relay publishes every business event to that queue.
sonnet.q2: Ingest reads the matching active subscriptions from the core DB and, in one delivery-DB transaction, inserts one `deliveries` row per match. `UNIQUE (event_id, subscription_id)` plus `ON CONFLICT (event_id, subscription_id) DO NOTHING` means a duplicate message inserts nothing new. It is then acked.
sonnet.q3: The signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<raw body>`, keyed with the subscription secret, where `t` is unix seconds. The header is `X-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`. It is built again at send time on every attempt, not once per delivery.
sonnet.q4: 2xx: status becomes `delivered`. 410: the delivery is dead-lettered, the subscription is set to `disabled` with `disabled_reason = 'gone'`, and all its pending and in_flight deliveries are swept to `dead`. Other 4xx: dead-lettered immediately, no retry. Transient failures (408, 429, any 5xx, timeout, connection error): retried with backoff while attempts remain, and dead-lettered on the 8th failure.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts. After the 2nd failure the 3rd attempt is made about 2 minutes later (with about 10% jitter).
sonnet.q6: In the `deliveries` table of the Delivery DB (our own Postgres). It holds `status`, `attempts`, `next_attempt_at`, `last_status_code` and `last_error`, plus the lease fields and timestamps.
sonnet.q7: It waits in the `deliveries` table with `status = 'pending'` and a future `next_attempt_at`. Each instance's dispatcher polls about every 1 s and claims rows whose `next_attempt_at <= now()`. That claim makes the attempt happen.
sonnet.q8: The row stays `in_flight` until its 30 s lease expires. Then any instance can reclaim it and send again, so the receiver may see a duplicate with the same `X-Webhook-Id`. The attempt was already counted at claim time. If the row already had 8 attempts, it is dead-lettered with `last_error = 'worker lost'` and not sent.
sonnet.q9: They are held in the same `deliveries` table with `status = 'dead'`, `dead_at` set and the last status code or error kept. Rows are purged after 14 days. A replay (`POST /deliveries/{id}/replay`) sets `status = 'pending'`, `attempts = 0` and `next_attempt_at = now()`, and clears `dead_at` and the last error. The delivery id is unchanged. It is refused with 409 while the subscription is disabled.
sonnet.q10: The `X-Webhook-Id` header, which is the delivery `id`. It does not change between retries or after a replay.
sonnet.q11: They are dead-lettered, not sent. They get `last_error = 'subscription disabled'`. They can be replayed once the subscription is re-enabled. The doc lists this as a decision that needs confirming.
sonnet.q12: Yes. The document says there is no ordering between events.
